ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB$ is a chord of the circle $\odot O$. Through point $O$, draw $OC\perp OA$, where $OC$ intersects $AB$ at $P$, and $CP=BC$. Point $Q$ lies on the arc $\overset{\frown}{AmB}$. $BC$ is a tangent line to the circle $\odot O$; Given that $\angle BAO=25^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle AQB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle BAO=25^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle ABO=25^\circ$, $\angle APO=65^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle POB=\angle APO-\angle ABO=40^\circ$,\\
therefore $\angle AQB=\frac{1}{2}(\angle AOP+\angle POB)=\frac{1}{2}\times 130^\circ=\boxed{65^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, with the center of the circle labeled O; A is above the circle, B is at the lower left of the circle, and Q is on the lower-right arc of the circle. Line segment AB is a chord of the circle, and OA and OB are radii from the center of the circle to points on the circle. Q is located at the position not containing the smaller arc subtended by chord AB, that is, on the arc on the other side of AB; therefore ∠AQB is an inscribed angle with arc AB as the subtended arc. Reasoning: Because OA=OB, triangle AOB is an isosceles triangle. Given ∠BAO=25°, so ∠ABO=25°. Therefore the central angle ∠AOB=180°-25°-25°=130°. ∠AQB is an inscribed angle, and what it subtends is arc AB, while the central angle corresponding to this arc is ∠AOB=130°, so ∠AQB=1/2×130°=65°.
